text: When you get paid through Razorpay, the money doesn't arrive order by order. Every two days you get one lump sum covering hundreds of orders, minus the gateway fee, minus eighteen percent G S T on that fee, minus any refunds netted out.
Someone in finance has to work backwards from that single bank credit and prove it matches what the books say. That is still substantially manual.
Razorpay's Optimizer already reconciles settlements against the bank. Moneta is the layer above: settlements against the merchant's own ledger. And unlike a rules engine, you can ask it why.

A hundred and twenty nine records, across nineteen settlement cycles. Ninety one point seven percent of value reconciled, in one point four milliseconds. That is the deterministic engine. There is no L L M anywhere in the matching path.
And this number here. Forty three thousand rupees, unresolved. I want to be direct about that, because a reconciliation tool that shows you a hundred percent is a tool that is hiding something.
Every exception is categorised and costed. Duplicate bookings, amount mismatches, missing entries, missing refunds.
And this panel is here on purpose. It renders even when it is empty. If Moneta cannot explain something, it says so on the front page, not in a log file.

The rules engine closed this one itself. Two sales vouchers, one payment. There is no ambiguity, so there is nothing to investigate. It is classified deterministically, and the evidence is right here.
The engine never asks a model whether two amounts are equal. Matching is integer comparison, in paise. A rules engine cannot hallucinate four thousand rupees into existence.

But these two, the engine could not close. It knows the amount is wrong on both. It just cannot say why. Two different settlements, three days apart. Same number, opposite signs. A rules engine sees two problems. It has no way to know they are one.
So let us ask it. Why doesn't settlement six four zero, seven seven one, five eight five, three five one match what we booked?

Watch what it is actually doing. It is not reasoning from memory. It is pulling the settlement, its line items and the merchant's vouchers through read only tools. Every number it is about to quote comes from a tool result, and the call it made is shown right there on screen.

And there it is. The merchant booked the gross payments straight to the bank and never accounted for the refund Razorpay netted out of that cycle. Five thousand nine hundred and forty four rupees, twenty four paise. The books and the bank were never going to agree.
That is a real reconciliation problem, and this is the part a rules engine structurally cannot do. It had to go and reconstruct where the money actually went.
And notice what it recommends. A journal entry, for a human to post. Moneta has eleven tools, and all eleven are reads. There is no write path to disable. It cannot touch the ledger, by construction.
A demo is one case. This is the whole held out set. A different seed, data the engine was never tuned on. The generator knows exactly which faults it injected, so we can score against ground truth.
Thirteen of thirteen injected faults, correctly attributed. Nothing missed. Nothing misclassified. Rules closed nine. The agent attributed the other four.

And here is where it fell short. Precision is ninety two point nine percent, not a hundred, because of one false positive. And it is the other half of the case I just showed you. It solved that settlement correctly, then labelled the mirror cycle a plain amount mismatch, instead of recognising it as the same refund. Right event, wrong label, on one of its two halves.
I am showing you that rather than netting it away. A held out score with the failures removed is not a score.
Every decision is on the record. Every match with its reason, every exception with its evidence, every tool call with its arguments. Append only J S O N lines.
If a finance team is going to trust this, they have to be able to reconstruct exactly how it reached a conclusion.

Razorpay's Optimizer reconciles settlements against the bank. Moneta reconciles them against the books. Hours of manual work per cycle, done in under a second, with a full audit trail, and complete honesty about what it could not resolve.
It is a closing and verification loop. It explains, it flags, and it never moves money.
